lessons.title: Memorization and Recitation (Nazira and Hifz)
lessons.notes_html:
Nazira Recitation

In Class 4, the first three parts (paras) of the Holy Quran are prescribed for Nazira recitation: Alif Laam Meem, Sayaqool and Tilkal Rusul.

  • One part is to be learnt in three months, and all three parts are completed in the academic year.
  • Out of the total 100 marks in Islamiat, 40 marks have been allocated for the Nazra section.
  • Success in Nazra Quran is compulsory for success in the Islamiat subject.

Surahs to Memorize (Hifz)

Surah Al-Kausar: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ ۝ فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ ۝ إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُ

Its simple meaning is: Allah Almighty has given the Nabi Karim (PBUH) Al-Kausar, that is, abundance of goodness. So we should pray to our Lord and offer sacrifice for Him alone. Surely, the enemy of the Prophet (PBUH) is the one who is cut off from all good.

Surah Al-Asr: وَالْعَصْرِ ۝ إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ ۝ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ

Its simple meaning is: By the time, surely man is in loss, except those who believe, do good deeds, advise one another to follow the truth and advise one another to be patient.

Surah Al-Ma'oon: أَرَءَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ ۝ فَذَٰلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ ۝ وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ ۝ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ ۝ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ ۝ الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ ۝ وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ

It tells us about the people who deny the Day of Judgment: they push away the orphan and do not urge feeding the poor. It also warns those who are careless about their Salah, who make a show of their deeds and who refuse to lend even small useful things to others.

Surah Al-Kafiroon: قُلْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا الْكٰفِرُونَ ۝ لَآ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ ۝ وَلَآ أَنتُمْ عٰبِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ ۝ وَلَآ أَنَا عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ ۝ وَلَآ أَنتُمْ عٰبِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ ۝ لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ

Its simple meaning is: Say, O disbelievers! I do not worship that which you worship, nor do you worship that which I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.

Memorization and Translation: Surah Al-Ikhlas

قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

Translation given in the book: O Nabi Karim (PBUH) say: Allah is the One (1). The Self-Sufficient Master (2). He begets not, nor was He begotten (3). And there is none co-equal or comparable to Him (4). This Surah teaches us the oneness of Allah Almighty.

Supplications with Meanings

  • سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ — "Subhana Rabbi-yal Azeem": Glory to my Allah the Exalted. It is recited in the Ruku (bowing) in Salah.
  • سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَىٰ — "Subhana Rabbi-yal Aala": O! Allah glory be to you, the most high. It is recited in the Sajdah (prostration) in Salah.
  • سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ — "Sami Allahu liman hamidah": Allah listens to him who praises Him. It is called Tasamia and is said while rising from Ruku.
  • رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ — "Rabbana lakal hamd": O! Our Allah, all praise is to you. It is called Tahmeed and is said after the Tasamia.
  • رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا — "Rabbi zidni ilma": O! Allah increase my knowledge. Students should recite this dua to pray for increase in knowledge.
  • جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا — "Jazak Allahu khairan": May Allah best reward you. We say this to thank a person who does a favour to us.

Key Points

  • This lesson is memorization and recitation: learn the three paras by reading (Nazira) and the small Surahs by heart (Hifz).
  • Surah Al-Ikhlas teaches the oneness of Allah Almighty.
  • The phrases of Ruku, Sajdah, Tasamia and Tahmeed are part of our daily Salah.

lessons.title: The Beliefs
lessons.notes_html:
The Basic Faiths of Islam

Believing in the following seven components of faith is compulsory for every Muslim:

  • (1) Faith in Allah Almighty
  • (2) Faith in Angels
  • (3) Faith in Divine Books
  • (4) Faith in Ambiya (Prophets)
  • (5) Faith in the Hereafter
  • (6) Faith in Fate
  • (7) Faith in revival of the life after death

Without even a single component, belief cannot exist.

Faith in Allah

Faith in Allah means to believe with a true heart that Allah Almighty is the Creator of this entire universe and the whole system of the universe is under His authority. He is One in His attributes and existence and none is equal to Him. He is free of every flaw and fault, and He is the possessor of life and death.

The Angels

Angels are the strong and luminous creatures of Almighty Allah, created from light. They do not need drinking, eating and sleeping. They only obey the command of Allah Almighty and never disobey. The four famous angels are:

  • Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) — conveys the messages of Allah Almighty to the Ambiya (AS).
  • Hazrat Michaeel (AS) — his responsibility is showing rain and blowing the winds.
  • Hazrat Izraeel (AS) — seizes the souls of all creatures.
  • Hazrat Israfeel (AS) — will blow the trumpet (Soor).

The Trumpet (Soor)

The trumpet is a luminous thing which Hazrat Israfeel (AS) has. He will blow it for the first time and the entire universe will come to an end. Then he will blow the trumpet a second time and everything will be restored to life. That day is called the Judgment Day.

Key Points

  • There are seven basic faiths of Islam; belief is incomplete without any one of them.
  • Allah Almighty created human beings for the trial and testing of their good deeds.
  • Hazrat Adam (AS) is the first of all the Ambiya (AS), and the Nabi Karim (PBUH) is the last of all Ambiya (AS).
  • The Holy Quran is preserved in its pure form.

mcqs.why: Allah Almighty is the possessor of life and death; He is One in His attributes and existence and none is equal to Him.

lessons.title: Pillars of Islam and Zakat
lessons.notes_html:
The Five Pillars of Islam

The structure of Islam is based on five pillars:

  • (1) Kalima-e-Tayyiba — affirming oneness of Allah and Risaalat
  • (2) Salah (Prayer)
  • (3) Zakat (Charity)
  • (4) Rozah (Fasting) in Ramazan
  • (5) Hajj (Pilgrimage)

The one who fulfills these pillars is called a Muslim. Kalima-e-Tayyiba is the first pillar of Islam.

Zakat

  • The literal meaning of Zakat is to be purified, increase or growth.
  • The Zakat obligated on land production is called Ushr.
  • Zakat is also obligated on a specified quantity of cattles.
  • Zakat was made obligatory after the migration to Madinah Munawwarah.

Who Is a Capable Person?

A capable person is the wealthy person who, other than his basic needs, has seven and a half tola (75 gram) gold or fifty-two and a half tola (520 gram) silver, or wealth of its equal price, and that wealth remained with him for a period of one year. Zakat becomes obligatory on such a person.

Advantages of Zakat

  • The wealth is increased and blessed by paying Zakat.
  • The poor and needy persons of the society are supported by Zakat.
  • Mutual love and affection is produced between the rich and the poor, and poverty is eliminated from the society.

Key Points

  • Islam means "to obey"; its structure stands on five pillars.
  • Zakat removes the worries of the poor and needy so they may satisfy their basic needs.

mcqs.q: On how many pillars is the structure of Islam based?
mcqs.why: The structure of Islam is based on five pillars: Kalima-e-Tayyiba, Salah, Zakat, Rozah in Ramazan, and Hajj. The one who fulfills these pillars is called a Muslim.

mcqs.why: Kalima-e-Tayyiba, affirming the oneness of Allah and Risaalat, is the first pillar of Islam.

mcqs.why: The Zakat obligated on land production is called Ushr, just as Zakat is obligatory on wealth and on a specified quantity of cattles.

mcqs.why: A capable person has seven and a half tola (75 gram) gold or fifty-two and a half tola (520 gram) silver, or wealth of its equal price, for a period of one year.

mcqs.why: The wealth must remain with the capable person for a period of one year; then Zakat becomes obligatory on such a person.

options: In the first year at Makkah

mcqs.why: Zakat was made obligatory after the migration to Madinah Munawwarah, so that the worries of the poor and needy persons may be removed.

options: To be purified, increase or growth
mcqs.why: The literal meaning of Zakat is to be purified, increase or growth.

mcqs.why: By paying Zakat the wealth is increased and blessed, the poor and needy are supported, and mutual love and affection is produced between the rich and the poor.

options: The poor and needy persons of the society
mcqs.why: The poor and needy persons of the society are supported through Zakat, so they may satisfy their basic needs.

mcqs.why: Just as Zakat is obligatory on wealth and Ushr on land production, in the same way Zakat is obligated on a specified quantity of cattles.

lessons.title: Allah's Rights
lessons.notes_html:
What Are Rights?

Rights means the responsibilities. According to Islamic teachings, these are the responsibilities that are on us and have to be fulfilled by us.

Allah's Rights

Allah's rights mean the responsibilities about Allah Almighty to be fulfilled by us. Being the Creator, Allah Almighty blessed the human countlessly, so all these blessings demand that human should obey Allah devotedly.

Allah's Rights on Us

  • Considering no partner of Allah in His existence and attributes
  • Offering pure devotion to Him and complying with His commands
  • Begging help from Him in every trouble and hardship
  • Loving Him above all
  • Keeping fear of His anger
  • Praying to Him only
  • Offering thanks on His blessings

Benefits of Fulfilling Allah's Rights

The person who fulfills Allah's rights with love and delight, Allah approves his prays (duas). Allah creates satisfaction and calmness for him in this world and in the hereafter, and he becomes successful in both the worlds.

Countless Blessings

Air, water, light, grain and fruit are extremely precious blessings of Allah Almighty, and these blessings are countless. Allah Almighty said: "If you (try to) count the bounties of Allah, you cannot count them all." [Ibrahim: 34] So surrendering ourselves completely to Him is Allah's right.

Key Points

  • We should be thankful to Allah and pray to Him only, to no one else.
  • Thanks should be offered on Allah's blessings.

mcqs.why: In the book's own exercise, 'Rights' means responsibility: the responsibilities that are on us and have to be fulfilled by us.

mcqs.why: Allah's blessings on human beings are countless. Allah said: 'If you (try to) count the bounties of Allah, you cannot count them all.' [Ibrahim: 34]

mcqs.why: Offering thanks on His blessings is one of Allah's rights on us, because He has blessed us countlessly.

mcqs.why: Praying to Him only is among Allah's rights on us; we should not pray to anyone else besides Allah Almighty.

mcqs.why: Allah's rights on us include keeping fear of His anger, loving Him above all, begging help from Him in every trouble, and praying to Him only.

mcqs.why: Begging help from Him in every trouble and hardship is one of Allah's rights on us, because He is our Creator and Master.

mcqs.why: Allah Almighty is our Creator and Master and He has blessed us countlessly; air, water, light, grain and fruit are extremely precious blessings of Allah.

options: He gives him a long life only
mcqs.why: The person who fulfills Allah's rights with love and delight, Allah approves his prays (duas) and creates satisfaction and calmness for him.

lessons.title: Human Rights
lessons.notes_html:
What Are Human Rights?

Human Rights means the rights of a person on the other. In the light of Islamic teachings, Allah Almighty may forgive His rights, but human beings' rights cannot be forgiven until the human himself forgives. For establishing peace and tranquility in the society, it is necessary to pay the rights of others properly and whole heartedly.

Parents' Rights Are the Most Important

Among human rights, the first and most important right is of parents. In the Holy Quran, Allah Almighty, after His obedience, ordered politeness for parents: "and do good to parents." [Al-Isra: 23] The parents must be obeyed in every permissible matter, looked at with respect and dignity, and we should keep on praying for the parents.

Whose Rights Must Be Fulfilled?

  • The rights of parents, children, relatives and friends are necessary to be fulfilled.
  • It is friend's right to behave with him with sincerity, and to support him in facing difficulties.
  • It is orphan's right to protect his wealth.
  • It is neighbour's right to consider his feelings; we should not do anything that hurts or troubles our neighbour.
  • It is relatives' right to be a partner in their happy and sad moments, and to behave nicely with them.
  • Taking care of the education and training of children is their right.

Double Reward

The Nabi Karim (PBUH) said about relatives: "Charity to poor is rewarded once, but charity to a needy relative is rewarded twice. One is for charity and the other is for treating the relative well." Brothers, sisters, uncles, nephews etc. are included in relatives.

Key Points

  • Allah Almighty will never forgive violation of human rights if the human beings themselves do not forgive, so human rights are much stressed.
  • Behaving politely and supporting the miserable, needy, traveler, helpless, distressed, poor and debtors are also included in human rights.

mcqs.q: Among human rights, which right is the first and most important?
mcqs.why: Among human rights, the first and most important right is of parents. In the Holy Quran, Allah, after His obedience, ordered politeness for parents. [Al-Isra: 23]

mcqs.why: The Nabi Karim (PBUH) said: 'Charity to poor is rewarded once, but charity to a needy relative is rewarded twice. One is for charity and the other is for treating the relative well.'

mcqs.q: What is the orphan's right?
mcqs.why: It is the orphan's right to protect his wealth; the home in which the orphan is patronized is a good home.

mcqs.q: What is the neighbour's right?
options: To consider his feelings and not hurt or trouble him
mcqs.why: It is the neighbour's right to consider his feelings, that is, we should not do anything that hurts or troubles our neighbour.

To give him gifts every day

mcqs.why: It is the friend's right to behave with him with sincerity, and to support him in facing difficulties; friends may not be behaved insincerely.

mcqs.q: When can human beings' rights be forgiven?
options: Only when the human himself forgives
mcqs.why: Allah Almighty may forgive His own rights if He wishes, but human beings' rights cannot be forgiven until the human himself forgives.

mcqs.q: In which Surah does Allah order 'and do good to parents'?
mcqs.why: The words 'and do good to parents' are from Surah Al-Isra, Ayat 23, where Allah, after His obedience, ordered politeness for parents.

mcqs.q: Whose rights are necessary to be fulfilled?
options: The rights of parents, children, relatives and friends
Only the rights of the poor
mcqs.why: The rights of parents, children, relatives and friends are necessary to be fulfilled; supporting the needy, traveler, helpless and poor is also included in human rights.

mcqs.q: Taking care of children, what is their right upon us?
mcqs.why: Taking care of the education and training of children is their right, as stated in the book's exercise.

mcqs.q: It is the relatives' right to be a partner in their:
mcqs.why: It is the relatives' right to be a partner in their happy and sad moments, and to behave nicely with them.

lessons.title: Divine Revelation
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Wahi?

The literal meaning of Wahi is to indicate secretly. According to Islamic teachings, Wahi is the orders of Allah Almighty which He reveals on His Ambiya (AS). The Wahi on Nabi Karim (PBUH) was revealed through Hazrat Jibraeel (AS).

The First Wahi

  • The first Wahi was revealed one night in the month of Ramazan.
  • Nabi Karim (PBUH) was busy in meditation in the cave Hira.
  • At the first revelation, Nabi Karim (PBUH) was at the age of forty.
  • Cave Hira is on Mountain Noor, at the distance of 3 miles from Makkah Mukarramah.

Hazrat Khadija (RA) Consoled Him

Hazrat Khadija (RA) consoled him and said: "I swear by Allah, He will not let you alone because you connect the relatives with relatives, help the people in difficulties, assist the poor, maintain hospitality with guests, and help the miserable people. That is why, Allah is with you in this important task." She believed in him at once.

Warqa bin Nofil

Hazrat Warqa bin Nofil, who was the scholar of the Zaboor and Gospel, affirmed it and said: "This is the angel who brought revelation (Wahi) to Hazrat Moosa (AS). If I were alive when your nation will drive you out of your homeland... If I remain alive, I would help you fully."

The First Revelation

The first revelation was the first five Ayat of Surah-e-Alaq. Translation: "Read with the name of your Lord who created (everything) [1]. He created man from a clot of blood [2]. Read, and your Lord is the most gracious [3], who imparted knowledge by means of the pen [4]. He taught man what he did not know [5]." [Al-Alaq: 1-5]

Key Points

  • Wahi is Allah's orders revealed to His Ambiya (AS) through Hazrat Jibraeel (AS).
  • Hazrat Khadija (RA) believed in Nabi Karim (PBUH) at once at the first revelation.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Wahi'?
mcqs.why: The literal meaning of 'Wahi' is to indicate secretly. According to Islamic teachings, Wahi is the orders of Allah Almighty which He reveals on His Ambiya (AS).

mcqs.q: In which month was the first Wahi revealed?
mcqs.why: The first Wahi was revealed one night in the month of Ramazan, when Nabi Karim (PBUH) was busy in meditation in the cave Hira.

mcqs.q: What was the age of Nabi Karim (PBUH) at the time of the first revelation?
mcqs.why: On the first revelation, Nabi Karim (PBUH) was at the age of forty, and Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) brought this first revelation in the cave Hira.

mcqs.q: At what distance is Cave Hira from Makkah Mukarramah?
mcqs.why: Cave Hira (Mountain Noor) is located at the distance of 3 miles from Makkah Mukarramah.

mcqs.q: Cave Hira is located on which mountain?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) brought the first revelation in the cave Hira, which is on Mountain Noor, 3 miles from Makkah Mukarramah.

mcqs.q: Through which angel was the Wahi revealed to Nabi Karim (PBUH)?
mcqs.why: The Wahi on Nabi Karim (PBUH) was revealed through Hazrat Jibraeel (AS), who conveys the messages of Allah Almighty to the Ambiya (AS).

mcqs.q: Hazrat Warqa bin Nofil was the scholar of which books?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Warqa bin Nofil was the scholar of the Zaboor and Gospel; he affirmed that the angel had also brought revelation to Hazrat Moosa (AS).

mcqs.q: The first revelation consisted of the first five Ayat of which Surah?
mcqs.why: The first revelation was the first five Ayat of Surah-e-Alaq: 'Read with the name of your Lord who created (everything)...' [Al-Alaq: 1-5]

mcqs.q: What was Nabi Karim (PBUH) doing in the cave Hira when the first Wahi came?
mcqs.why: Nabi Karim (PBUH) remained busy in the cave Hira in meditation, as the book's own exercise confirms.

mcqs.q: What did Hazrat Khadija (RA) do at the first revelation?
options: She consoled Nabi Karim (PBUH) and believed in him at once

lessons.title: The Preaching of Islam
lessons.notes_html:
The First Believers

Hazrat Khadija (RA) embraced Islam first of all; she believed in Nabi Karim (PBUH) at once at the first revelation. At the early stage:

  • From among children: Hazrat Ali (RA)
  • From among slaves: Hazrat Zaid bin Harisa (RA)
  • From among friends: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)

The period of secret preaching in Makkah Mukarramah was three years.

Invitation to the Close Relatives

Nabi Karim (PBUH) invited his Abdul Muttalib family on a meal. After the meal, he preached Islam to the family members and asked who will support him. Hazrat Ali (RA), who was about 10 years of age at that time, said: "Though I am a child but I will support you," and Nabi Karim (PBUH) embraced him.

Open Preaching from Mountain Safa

Allah's command was revealed: "And warn the nearest people of your clan." [Al-Shu'raa: 214] and "Now, proclaim what you are commanded to, and turn away from those who ascribe partners to Allah." [Al-Hijr: 94] After these orders, Nabi Karim (PBUH) started preaching Islam openly. It was the Arab's tradition that in case of any threatening situation a person used to call the people by climbing up the hill Safa, so he climbed the mountain of Safa and called the names of each tribe.

He said: "If I say you that there is an army behind this mountain, ready to attack you, would you believe me?" All said: "Yes, because you never told a lie." Then Nabi Karim (PBUH) preached about the oneness of Allah and said: "I am the warner to you about Allah's punishment."

Opposition

The Quraish became angry, and especially Abu Lahab opposed Nabi Karim (PBUH) harshly. He talked rudely and said: "Have you gathered us for this?" The polytheists of Makkah Mukarramah and the idolaters started persecuting the Muslims.

Key Points

  • In the beginning, Nabi Karim (PBUH) invited his nearest friends to Islam.
  • From among the women, Hazrat Khadija (RA) embraced Islam first.

lessons.title: The Firmness of Nabi Karim (PBUH) against the opposition of Quraish
lessons.notes_html:
Truthful and Trustworthy

Before the announcement of Risaalat, the people of Makkah Mukarramah respected Nabi Karim (PBUH) greatly and called him truthful and trustworthy. But when he called them towards the worship of One Allah and prohibited them from the worship of the idols, they became his bitter opponents.

Persecution of Hazrat Bilal (RA)

Hazrat Bilal-e-Habashi (RA) was the slave of Ummayah bin Khalaf. When he accepted Islam, Ummayah laid him down on the hot sand, put a heavy stone on his chest and asked him to reject Islam; but even in huge pain Hazrat Bilal (RA) chanted "Allah Ahad" (Allah is One). Eventually Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) got him free by purchasing him.

Persecution of Hazrat Khabbab (RA)

Hazrat Khabbab Bin Al-Arat (RA) was laid down on the burning coals and a man put the feet on his chest; the burning coals damped of his melting grease, and this made his whole back spotful.

Tricks of the Quraish

The Quraish used every trick against Nabi Karim (PBUH). They called him mad and magician, talked to him indecently, spread thorns in his way, and dragged him harshly covering his neck with a coverlet. Once, at the instigation of Abu Jahal, the guts of a camel were thrown on him while he was offering Salah in Khana-e-Ka'aba; Hazrat Fatima (RA) removed the guts from his neck. They also complained to his uncle Hazrat Abu Talib to stop his nephew from preaching, and they treated the believers cruelly.

The Firm Answer

Hazrat Abu Talib called him and said: "O my nephew, do not overburden me." Nabi Karim (PBUH) said to his uncle: "I Swear by Allah! If these people put the sun on my right hand and the moon on the left, even then I would continue my preaching till the spread of Islam, or I may pass away in spreading Islam."

The First Lady Martyr

Hazrat Sumayya (RA) was the first lady martyred in the way of Islam. She was the mother of Hazrat Ammar Bin Yasir (RA); when she accepted Islam, Abu Jahal tortured and martyred her with a spear.

Key Points

  • Despite the opposition of the unbelievers, Nabi Karim (PBUH) continued his preaching, and Islam kept on spreading.

lessons.title: Migration to Habsha (Ethiopia)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Migration (Hijrat)

According to the teachings of Islam, the literal meaning of Migration (Hijrat) is leaving a place where one cannot follow the religion freely, and to leave for a peaceful land where the religion may be followed without any restriction. A Muslim always remains prepared to sacrifice even his dearest thing, and remains ready to migrate if he faces difficulty in following the religion.

Habsha and Its King

Habsha is an African country, presently called Ethiopia. Its king was called Negus (Najashi) at that time, and he was a kind hearted and virtuous king.

Why Did the Muslims Migrate?

When the persecution of the unbelievers increased on the Muslims in Makkah Mukarramah, Allah commanded Nabi Karim (PBUH) to say to the Muslims: "It is better for you to migrate towards Habsha, where the king is kind hearted and virtuous, and not cruel, therefore you should stay till Allah Almighty remove your trouble." So the Muslims migrated to Habsha to protect themselves from persecution and to follow their religion in peace.

  • There were fifteen Muslims in the first migration to Habsha.
  • There were one hundred and one Muslims in the second migration to Habsha.
  • Hazrat Usman (RA) was accompanied with his wife Hazrat Ruqayya (RA) in the first migration to Habsha.

In Najashi's Court

Hazrat Ja'far Tayyaar (RA), the cousin of Nabi Karim (PBUH), represented the Muslims in Najashi's court. He delivered an impressive speech and, on the king's asking, recited few Ayat from Surah-e-Maryam, in which the detail of Hazrat Eisa (AS) and his respected mother is mentioned; by listening to Allah's Ayahs, Najashi became tearful.

The Quraish Delegation

The Quraish sent two wise men, Abdullah bin Rabeeaa and Amr bin Al-Aas, to Najashi along with precious gifts, asking him to hand over the Muslims. But Najashi was a just and wise king; he called the Muslims to hear their point of view and, in the end, reassured them that they can live in the country peacefully.

Key Points

  • Migration is for the sake of following the religion freely and in peace.
  • Najashi refused to hand over the Muslims to the Quraish.

lessons.title: Besiegement in Shi'b Abi Talib and the Year of Sorrow
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Shi'b Abi Talib?

Shi'b means the narrow land or valley between two mountains. This valley belonged to the Banu Hashim family, which was headed by Hazrat Abu Talib, due to which the valley was called Shi'b Abi Talib.

The Cruel Agreement

In the agreement, the chiefs of Makkah Mukarramah pledged that: negotiation with Banu Hashim is no more; no one will make any business with them; no one will do marriage contracts with them; and they will be cut off until they handover Nabi Karim (PBUH) to them. They prepared this agreement jointly and hanged it on the wall of Khana-e-Ka'aba. This event occurred in the 7th year of Nabuwwat.

Difficulties in the Valley

All the men, women and children of the Banu Hashim family went into the valley carrying eating items with them. When the eating items were finished off, they remained hungry for days, and they survived by eating tree leaves and leather pieces. Nabi Karim (PBUH) and his companions remained in this situation for three years.

How the Agreement Ended

Allah Almighty helped the Muslims in the way that the agreement hanged on the wall of Ka'aba was eaten by termite. Besides, Hisham bin Amr also condemned the chiefs of Makkah Mukarramah that the agreement was a cruel act. So the agreement was broken off in the 10th year of Nabuwwat, and Nabi Karim (PBUH) and his associates came out of the besiege.

The Year of Sorrow

The 10th year of Nabuwwat is called the year of sorrow, because in this year the uncle of Nabi Karim (PBUH), Hazrat Abu Talib, and his loyal wife Hazrat Khadija (RA) died. They both not only sacrificed their wealth to Nabi Karim (PBUH) but also put their lives in danger and kept on helping and supporting him.

Key Points

  • The besiegement in Shi'b Abi Talib remained for three years.
  • The 10th year of Nabuwwat brought both the end of the besiegement and the year of sorrow.

lessons.title: Journey to Taa'if
lessons.notes_html:
Why Taa'if?

When the people of Makkah Mukarramah not only refused to accept the invitation of Nabi Karim (PBUH) to Islam but they also persecuted him, then Nabi Karim (PBUH) intended to preach the people of Taa'if, so that the message of Islam may reach new people. This event occurred in the 10th year of Prophethood.

The Companion and the City

Nabi Karim (PBUH) brought his freed slave Hazrat Zaid bin Harisa (RA) with him in this journey. The city Taa'if is located at the distance of 70 miles from the south of Makkah Mukarramah and was very famous for its gardens and meadows.

The Chiefs of Taa'if

There was a strong tribe Banu Saqeef in Taa'if, which was headed by three most famous chiefs: Abd Yaleel, Masood and Habeeb. They were brothers. Nabi Karim (PBUH) first of all preached these three chiefs.

The Cruel Treatment

The chiefs not only refused him, but ridiculed him; one of them said: "Did God not find anyone else to choose him as a Prophet?" Then they hounded wanderers and mischievous boys after him, who taunted him and threw stones on him. He was made seriously injured, and even his shoes soaked with blood.

Addas Accepts Islam

The Christian servant Addas brought a bunch of grapes to Nabi Karim (PBUH) in the garden. After knowing the teachings of Nabi Karim (PBUH), Addas accepted Islam.

The Prophet's Dua for Taa'if

When Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) came with the angel of mountains and said that if he wished, the angel would destroy the people of Taa'if by grinding them between the two mountains, Nabi Karim (PBUH) said: "No, I hope that if they do not accept, but their offspring will accept and worship Allah." Then Nabi Karim (PBUH) offered dua for them: "O Allah! Guide them because they don't know."

Key Points

  • Nabi Karim (PBUH) was teased much in the journey of Taa'if, yet he prayed for the guidance of its people.
  • The people will be raised from the offspring of Taa'if who will believe in Allah and worship Him.

lessons.title: The Ascension of Nabi Karim (PBUH)
lessons.notes_html:
The Two Parts of the Ascension

  • (1) Isra — the journey from Masjid-e-Haraam to Masjid-e-Aqsa (Palestine). At Masjid-e-Aqsa, all the Ambiya (AS) had been gathered and Nabi Karim (PBUH) led the congregational Salah.
  • (2) Mairaaj (Ascension) — the remaining journey, from Masjid-e-Aqsa to the heavens and to Sidra-tul-Muntaha, and to the extent Allah Almighty wished. In the heavens, he met various Prophets and was shown the reward and punishment of good and evil acts.

Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) accompanied him to Sidra-tul-Muntaha, from where Nabi Karim (PBUH) went himself to the next destination, got the blessed nearness of Allah Almighty and had an honoured conversation with Allah Almighty. On this occasion, Allah rewarded him the priceless gift of Salah.

When and How It Happened

The event of ascension occurred in the 12th year of Nabuwwat. One night, when Nabi Karim (PBUH) was sleeping, Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) came with a white animal called Burraq, bigger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, on which Nabi Karim (PBUH) rode and came to Masjid-e-Aqsa.

In the Holy Quran

The event of ascension and Isra is described in Surah-e-Bani Israeel. The first part of the journey is mentioned in its first Ayat: "Glorious is He Who made his servant travel by night from Masjid-ul-Haram to Masjid-ul-Aqsa." [Bani Israeel: 1]

Key Points

  • Ascension means the blessed journey of Nabi Karim (PBUH) arranged by Allah Almighty.
  • Salah was obligated on the occasion of ascension.
  • The literal meaning of ascension is ladder or an instrument to ascend by.

lessons.title: Migration to Madinah Munawwarah
lessons.notes_html:
Yasrib Becomes Madinat-u-Nabi

The old name of Madinah Munawwarah was Yasrib. When Nabi Karim (PBUH) migrated here, the Muslims named it Madinat-u-Nabi (The City of the Prophet). Madinah Munawwarah is located at the distance of two hundred seventy five miles (442 km), in the North of Makkah Mukarramah.

The Journey

The unbelievers planned to murder Nabi Karim (PBUH); Abu Jahal suggested that one person from each tribe remain prepared to attack. Allah Almighty allowed Nabi Karim (PBUH) to migrate. He decided to accompany Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) with him, and before migration he handed over the trusts of the unbelievers to Hazrat Ali (RA) and ordered him to return the deposited things to their owners.

The unbelievers besieged his house, but by Allah's help he came out safely and departed. As a strategy, they remained in the cave Soar (Thawr) for three days, where Hazrat Abu Bakr's (RA) slave Hazrat Amir bin Fuhaira (RA) and his daughter Hazrat Asma (RA) brought meal and goat's milk for them. The unbelievers announced the prize of 100 camels for arresting him; Suraqa bin Ju'shum searched and found them, but his horse stumbled again and again, so he became regretful, apologized, and he was forgiven.

Quba: The First Masjid of Islam

Nabi Karim (PBUH) reached the town Quba, near Madinah Munawwarah, stayed there for 14 days, and founded here the very first Masjid of Islam, remembered as Masjid-e-Quba. Then he reached Madinah Munawwarah, where he was welcomed warmly and little girls sang a song of praise in his honour.

Three Important Tasks in Madinah

  • (1) He founded Masjid-e-Nabawi and participated himself in its construction.
  • (2) He associated the migrants of Makkah with the residents of Madinah as brothers; this relationship is called Muwaakhaat. The people of Madinah (Ansaar) helped the empty hand Migrants (Muhajireen).
  • (3) He made a written treaty with the Jews of Madinah, called Meesaq-e-Madinah Munawwarah, the first written constitution of the newly established Islamic state.

Key Points

lessons.title: Honesty
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Honesty?

According to Islamic teachings, honesty means to fulfill any right of anyone properly. It means that carrying out all assigned tasks according to the orders of Allah Almighty and His Nabi Karim (PBUH) is honesty. Allah Almighty commands: "Surely, Allah commands you to deliver trusts to those entitled to them." [Al-Nisa: 58]

The Scope of Honesty

Generally, people consider honesty limited to financial rights, but its scope is broader; honesty is related to all the matters of life. For example:

  • Returning someone's entrusted property completely
  • Keeping someone's secret intact
  • Giving right advice to someone on his request
  • Performing the assigned duties truly
  • Appointing meritorious people on public posts
  • Correct use of time and getting education whole heartedly

Honesty and Education

Correct use of time and getting education whole heartedly is honesty with the self and with the nation. A student who studies honestly, uses his time correctly and fulfills the right of his teachers and books is an honest student. Without honesty, education cannot give its true benefit.

The Merchant Who Cheated

Once, Nabi Karim (PBUH) observed that a merchant mixed water with the grain to make it heavier. Nabi Karim (PBUH) said: "He who cheats us is none of us." This Hadith teaches us that cheating in trade is against honesty.

The Example of Nabi Karim (PBUH)

The life of Nabi Karim (PBUH) is a great and excellent example of honesty. Even his bitter enemies entrusted their belongings to him, and the people called him Ameen (the trustworthy). At the time of migration, he handed over their trusts to Hazrat Ali (RA) so that he may handover to their owners.

Key Points

  • One who does not fulfill the trust has not any faith.
  • The heart of the honest remains content and satisfied.
  • Honesty increases human's dignity and respect.

lessons.title: Simplicity
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Simplicity?

Simplicity means a life having neither extravagance nor stinginess. Allah Almighty says: "And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor miserly, and it (i.e. their spending) is moderate in between (the two extremes)." [Al-Furqaan: 67] Simplicity is the key attribute of a Muslim. Nabi Karim (PBUH) said: "Simple life is the sign of faith."

Simplicity of Nabi Karim (PBUH)

  • He never constructed a big house for him; few belongings were there in his home and a leather bed filled with date's peel.
  • He used the bread of unstrained flour.
  • He disliked taking meal in gold and silver crockery.
  • He wore simple but clean dress and used to patch his dresses himself.
  • He disliked ceremonial food and never found defects in meals.
  • He used to cooperate in doing household tasks with family members.
  • He arranged a very simple marriage of his dear daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).

Simplicity of the Companions

Hazrat Umar (RA) wore the patched dresses, and he strictly instructed his governors not to wear silky and tight dress and not to live a luxurious life. Despite being wealthy, Hazrat Usman (RA) lived a simple life, and Hazrat Ali (RA) also lived a simple life.

Importance and Benefits of Simplicity

The nation that adopts simplicity makes progress and never becomes dependent on other nations. The nation that involves in luxurious life becomes financially weak and dependent on other nations. The benefits of simplicity are: a person and a nation make progress; they never become dependent on anyone; the nation remains financially strong; and real peace and tranquility is obtained in life.

Key Points

  • Simplicity does NOT mean stinginess; it means moderate spending.
  • The secret of a nation's progress and development is also based on simplicity.

lessons.title: Social Work
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Social Work?

Social work means to serve Allah's creature without any discrimination. According to a Hadith, "The creature is Allah's family"; this is why serving people is also a worship. Serving people is the most important and rewarding work after Allah's worship and good treatment with parents.

Examples from the Life of Nabi Karim (PBUH)

  • He maintained good behavior to all without any discrimination; even when the non-Muslims fell ill, Nabi Karim (PBUH) visited them to enquire their health.
  • Once a poor man came to him; Nabi Karim (PBUH) gave many goats to him for the pleasure of Allah Almighty.
  • He also used to visit Hazrat Khabab's (RA) home to milk the goats, because no one in his home was for milking.

Forms of Social Work

Every work that removes trouble of the people and provides peace and comforts to them is a social work: fulfilling the needs of the needy people, helping the distressed people, offering sympathy to grieved people, cooperating with orphans, widows, poor and travelers, feeding up the hungry persons, and arranging education and training for the poor. Establishing welfare institutions, like charitable hospitals, Masajid and educational institutions, is also social work, and these are called continuing charity.

Benefits of Social Work

Serving the people sincerely is the most approved and admired act after the worship of Allah Almighty. This makes Allah pleased and people get rid of the hardship. It produces sympathetic emotions among the people for one another, which leads to a peaceful and satisfied and progressive society. The prime form of social work is to feed the poor, needy and orphans.

Examples of the Companions (RA)

  • Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to feed an old lady the bread by making it soft, before caliphate and even after the caliphate.
  • Hazrat Umar Farooque (RA) often kept patrolling the streets and towns in the nights to take care of the people; once he helped a lady suffering of labour pain by bringing his wife along with necessary things.
  • Hazrat Usman (RA) bought a well of drinking water and devoted it for the Muslims and other common people of Madinah Munawwarah.
  • Hazrat Ali (RA) used to break the fast (Iftaar) himself with dates and give his share of meal to the poor.

Key Points

  • Establishing an educational institution is also social work, a form of continuing charity.
  • Through social work, the society gets peace and comfort.

lessons.title: Social Etiquettes
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Gathering?

Majlis (social gathering) means gathering of the people at a place. Allah Almighty created the human beings in a way they like and prefer gatherings; they cannot live in this world alone.

Why Do People Arrange Gatherings?

People arrange different types of gatherings and meetings so that new ways of progress and development may be found out, firmness in the knowledge and faith may be obtained, problems may be solved, and time with friends may be spent. These gatherings have great importance when the necessary rules and manners are observed.

How a Gathering Should Be Started

A meeting should be started with the name of Allah, so that Allah's blessings may encompass the gathering. On joining a gathering, we should first salute and pay compliments and respect to the people around by saying "Aslam-o-alaikum" (peace be upon you).

Social Etiquettes

  • Salute the sitting people by saying "Aslam-o-alaikum" before having a seat in the gathering.
  • Do not interrupt others while speaking, but wait for your turn.
  • The elders should be respected in the gathering.
  • The sitting people should provide a place to the people coming in the gathering.
  • Arriving people should sit where there is a place to sit easily, and should not strive for sitting in the front row by crossing over the sitting people.
  • We should not sit in others' place by making them stand; rather, providing your place to others is an admired act.
  • The matters of a secret gathering should not be disclosed; we should keep them intact.

Key Points

  • Gathering means a group of people sitting together at a place.
  • Start the gathering or meeting with the name of Allah.

lessons.title: Time Management
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Time Management?

Time management means to do the tasks exactly at the time for which it was set. One should not leave today's tasks for tomorrow, but carry out the task with proper planning. A good student always makes a time management plan for his sleeping, awakening, study, playing and household tasks, and implements the time plan for each task timely.

Advantages of Time Management

Time management is essential for a peaceful and successful life. All the wealth that a person earns is just because of time management, and the person who maintains the time management can live a successful life. The great people of past time were very punctual towards their tasks, and they truly valued the time.

Loss of Wasting Time

According to an Arabic saying, "Wasting time is actually wasting yourself". The people who waste their time, actually the time wastes them, and they become failed at every point of their life. No one can reverse or return the time passed, and it would be asked about time on the Day of Judgment also, especially about the time spent during the period of youth. Time is a very precious and powerful thing; a good Muslim never wastes his time.

The Quran About Time

Allah Almighty says: "Surely, Salah is an obligation on the believers that is tied up with time." [Al-Nisa: 103] The Holy Quran also tells this attribute of the beloved followers of Allah Almighty: "and when they pass by the absurd things, pass by them with dignity." [Al-Furqaan: 72]

Wisdom Behind Timed Worship

This entire universe created by Allah Almighty is based on the principle of time management; the Sun, the Moon and the earth are all moving in their orbits at set timing. Similarly, Allah Almighty has set the time for His worship also, to teach Muslims to value time and make the habit of time management. Azaan, Roza, Hajj and Zakaat are also based on time management.

Key Points

  • Every task should be done on its time; the time that is passed cannot be reversed.
  • A good human being does not waste his time.

lessons.title: Love the Country and the Fellow Countrymen
lessons.notes_html:
Country and Countrymen

Country is an area of land having territorial boundaries, whereas the people in the country are called Countrymen. Our well-being and progress is well-connected with our country. To love the country and fellow-countrymen is a natural spirit, and it exists in every human being without any discrimination. Our safety lies in the security of our country; if our country is secure, we are secured as well.

Ways of Love to Country and Fellow-Countrymen

  • (1) Forget mutual differences, think above religious, linguistic and regional differences, and be proud of being Muslims and Pakistanis.
  • (2) Work hard day and night in our respective places and serve our country and fellow-countrymen with integrity and purity.
  • (3) Respect each other without discrimination, use and save the country's resources, like electricity, water and gas, appropriately, and make justice our habit.

We should think and act positively for the people living in our country, and avoid every act that is harmful for our country and its inhabitants. Whenever our country's safety and security is threatened, we should defend it with loyalty.

Patriotism of Nabi Karim (PBUH)

When our beloved Nabi Karim (PBUH) was migrating from his native city Makkah Mukarramah, he said good-bye with tearful eyes. At departure time, Nabi Karim (PBUH) said to Makkah Mukarramah: "O Makkah! I love you, but your residents have made it hard for me to live here." This shows his deep love for his homeland.

Key Points

  • The country and fellow-countrymen are our strength and stability.
  • We should adopt justice and fairness in our personalities and avoid injustice to anyone.

lessons.title: Hazrat Musa (AS)
lessons.notes_html:
Family and Nation

The name of Hazrat Musa's (AS) father was Imran, who belonged to the Bani Israeel tribe. Hazrat Musa (AS) is one of the dignified Ambiya (AS) of Allah Almighty, through whom Allah liberated the Bani Israeel from Pharaoh. Hazrat Musa (AS) was born about three thousand and five hundred years before Nabi Karim (PBUH).

Israeel is the title of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS), and Bani Israeel means the offspring of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS). Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) migrated from Palestine to Egypt in the reign of his son Hazrat Yousuf (AS) and settled there.

Pharaoh's Cruelty and the Birth of Hazrat Musa (AS)

Pharaoh, out of his arrogance, compelled people to worship and prostrate to him; he claimed of being God, but Bani Israeel refused to prostrate and worship Pharaoh (Firoun). Pharaoh ordered that every boy child born in Bani Israeel must be killed and the girls kept alive, because a Qibti astrologer had told him that a child in Banu Israeel will be born and become the cause of the fall of his government.

When Hazrat Musa (AS) was born, his mother put him in a box and floated it in the River Nile, trusting Allah Almighty; the box reached to Pharaoh's palace, where Bibi Asiya decided to adopt the child.

Two Miracles of Hazrat Musa (AS)

  • The first was the miraculous staff, which when thrown on the surface became a serpent.
  • The second miracle was the bright hand: when he put his hand under the arm and brought it out, it became luminous.

Key Points

  • Hazrat Musa (AS) was bestowed with Nabuwwat on returning from Madyan.
  • Hazrat Haroon (AS) was also bestowed Nabuwwat by the dua of Hazrat Musa (AS).

lessons.title: Hazrat Umar (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Title and Family

The title of Hazrat Umar (RA) was Farooque and his surname was Abu Hafs. His father's name was Khattab and he belonged to the noble branch of Bani Addi tribe. Farooque means the one who distinguishes between right and wrong. Nabi Karim (PBUH) rewarded him the title Farooque because, by his conversion to Islam, the difference between right and wrong became clear to the people.

Hazrat Umar (RA) had great intelligence and a dominating (impressive) personality, so the Quraish handed over embassy to him and he solved complex issues with great intelligence and wisdom as an ambassador. His daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the honourable wife of Nabi Karim (PBUH).

Acceptance of Islam

Nabi Karim (PBUH) especially prayed for Hazrat Umar's (RA) entrance into Islam: "O Allah, honor Islam with one of the two men, either by ibn Hasham or by ibn Al-Khattab." Allah Almighty accepted this pray, and Hazrat Umar (RA) accepted Islam in the 6th year of the Nabuwwat. When Hazrat Umar (RA) heard Quranic Ayat he spontaneously said "La ilaha illallah" (There is no god but Allah), and accepted Islam.

Courage After His Islam

Till that time, nearly forty people had become Muslims, but they had not courage to worship openly. After Hazrat Umar's (RA) entry into Islam, Nabi Karim (PBUH) was not afraid of anyone and he offered Salah in Khana-e-Ka'aba. Islam got strength by Hazrat Umar's (RA) conversion to Islam, and open preaching of Islam began.

Achievements of the Farooqi Period

  • Establishment of advisory council (Shura)
  • Establishment of Irrigation department
  • Promoting public treasury system
  • Establishing Army as institution
  • Appointment of salaried teachers in education department
  • Construction of Masajid abundantly in all cities
  • The conquests of Iran, Bait-ul-Muqaddas and Iraq

The period of Hazrat Umar's (RA) caliphate remained for ten years and few months. In the matter of justice and fairness, his caliphate is regarded as a model not only in Muslims but also in non-Muslim nations. He was martyred by a Persian slave, Ferouz Abu Lo'Lo.

Key Points

  • After the demise of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hazrat Umar (RA) was assigned the task of caliphate.
  • Hazrat Umar (RA) attained excellence in horse riding and wrestling.
